classifiedFindings.label: H-01
classifiedFindings.title: NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor settles a staker's pending phUSD with _safePay, paying the MIGRATOR while emitting Claimed(user, …)

classification.assetImpact: A migrated user's fully-accrued (matured) phUSD reward is transferred to the migrator contract instead of the user. On the InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator path it is recoverable by owner rescueERC20 (manual hand-distribution). On the NFTStakerMigrator path it is PERMANENTLY LOST — that contract has no rescueERC20, no rescueERC1155, no fallback and no receive (DEDUP-20-010). PoC testD confirms 82,191.78 phUSD permanently stranded.
attackPath: 1. No attacker is required. This is the ordinary, intended operational path.
2. Operator initiates a cross-staker migration whose orchestrator is NFTStakerMigrator.
3. Orchestrator calls NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor(user, …) (onlyMigrator).

4. depositFor settles the user's pending reward via _safePay, which forwards to _safePayTo(msg.sender, …). Because depositFor is onlyMigrator, msg.sender is ALWAYS the orchestrator and NEVER the user.
5. The full pending balance lands on NFTStakerMigrator; Claimed(user, amount) is emitted anyway, so off-chain reconciliation reports the user was paid.
6. NFTStakerMigrator exposes no recovery function of any kind. The phUSD is unrecoverable by anyone, including the owner.
classification.likelihood: high on the affected path — deterministic, not probabilistic. Every migrated user who already held a position on the target pool loses their entire accrued balance on that call. Mitigating timing fact: neither migrator is deployed today, so present on-chain exposure is zero.
classification.assumptions: The user being migrated already holds a position on the target pool (otherwise pending == 0 and nothing is misrouted). The migration is run through NFTStakerMigrator rather than InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the operator running the documented migration. No attacker, no market conditions, no privileged misuse.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 High: 'assets can be stolen/LOST/compromised'. Loss counts, and this is loss of MATURED yield, which project law treats as equivalent to capital loss (unmatured/in-motion yield is what caps at Medium; this is settled, pending, owed). There are no hand-wavy hypotheticals: the path is the intended one, the PoC is 4/4 PASS with a genuine control (testB proves batchMigrate pays correctly, so the defect is path-specific rather than a blanket claim), and the loss is terminal because the receiving contract has no recovery primitive whatsoever. The defect is a known-and-named bug: story-021's own commit body identifies '_safePay … which would pay the migrator', its ported NatSpec calls the _safePay form 'wrong in every case', and the fix was written into the new fourth copy (NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:887) while NFTStakerDepletion.sol was explicitly left untouched.
classifiedFindings.whyNotMedium: The four grounds offered for Medium do not survive weighing. (a) 'No attacker required or benefits' is not a mitigant for a loss finding — it removes the adversarial precondition and therefore RAISES likelihood to deterministic. (b) 'Magnitude bounded by pending accrued' is a bound, not a smallness claim: the PoC measures 82,191.78 phUSD, which is not dust. (c) 'Solvency invariant not broken' means the protocol stays solvent while individual users are made whole-less — protocol solvency is not the asset at issue. (d) 'Neither migrator is deployed' bounds PRESENT EXPOSURE, not the severity of the code as written, and pre-deployment is precisely when a self-audit has leverage.

classifiedFindings.label: M-02
classifiedFindings.title: Duplicate rewardTokens entries pay the same pre-loop snapshot k times and recapture the batch's own donations
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessLabel: F-20-01 (story-unsafe — §4.5 contradicts §4.2 inside the same normative document; Law-1 override applies)

classification.assetImpact: Protocol-directed incentive funds (StableYieldAccumulator nudgeSplit drip + BalancerPoolerV2 per-mint cut) leak back to the batcher that generated them. The donate-forward mechanic that docs/multi-token-nudge.md §4.2 calls load-bearing is defeated: a batcher recaptures up to ~100% of their own batch's donation and can drive the next claimant's seed to zero. No user principal is at risk.
attackPath: 1. _snapshotRewards writes the same pre-loop balance B into every duplicate slot of the caller-supplied rewardTokens array.
2. The mint loop raises the live balance by the batch's own donation D (the pinned dispatcher donates on every mint).
3. _payRewards transfers snapshot[i] once per array element with no cumulative per-token cap.
4. k transfers succeed whenever k*B <= B+D, so the caller is paid k times out of a pot that was counted once.
5. Back-to-back batches nullify donate-forward permanently: prior pot 77.64 USDC, paid out 155.28, 0 left behind.
classification.likelihood: medium — permissionless (any caller supplies the array), no privilege, no timing. Bounded by the batch's own donation size: at count=400 the mainnet shape gives k=9 and 704.53 of 776.40 USDC clawed back (≈90.7% self-recapture). Honest bound: at the CURRENTLY OBSERVED mainnet shape the duplicate path still fails closed (test_AtObservedShape_DuplicateStillFailsClosed) — it needs a large batch to bite.
classification.assumptions: The pinned dispatcher donates a legal reward asset to the batcher on each mint. True today: DISPATCHER_INDEX=4, BalancerPoolerV2, primeToken()==USDS, forwards a USDC cut, so USDC is simultaneously a legal reward token and a per-mint donation.
classification.externalRequirements: A batch large enough that k*B <= B+D. Corroborating incident lineage recorded at tx 0x6d71d6fd, block 25242986.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Medium. classifiedFindings.label: M-03
classifiedFindings.title: POSSIBLE INCOMPLETE FIX of ledger M-01 — migrateIn slice ordering reaches the linear-depletion rate-drift class through the migration path

classification.assetImpact: Value transfer between users out of a shared reward budget. On NFTStakerDepletion the emission rate = budget / windowSeconds is INDEPENDENT of totalStaked, so slice-1 users split the ENTIRE pool-wide emission stream among themselves while every later slice sits parked in the migrator earning nothing. Measured: slice-1 user receives 120% of the slice-2 user (48,977.29e18 vs 40,758.11e18) over identical wall-clock exposure.
attackPath: 1. Operator calls finalizeAndReset (requires totalStaked == 0), which drains the depletion pool.
2. Emissions resume the instant slice 1 is re-injected via migrateIn -> depositFor.
3. Because rate is independent of totalStaked, the handful of slice-1 users receive the FULL pool-wide stream rather than their pro-rata share.
4. Slice-N users remain in the migrator's custody, accruing nothing, while their share of the shared rewardBudget is consumed.
5. Payout is decided entirely by which slice the operator assigned a user to — a variable no user controls and none can observe in advance.
classification.likelihood: certain on any staggered migration of this contract. No attacker; the operator's ordinary slice ordering is the trigger. A clean remedy exists (setTargetAPY(0) immediately after finalizeAndReset, restore after the last slice) but it is not currently a documented runbook step.
classification.assumptions: The migration is executed in more than one slice, which is the expected shape (ECON_C measures ~426 users per 30M-gas block, so multi-slice is required above that).

classifiedFindings.justification: Classified MEDIUM, matching ledger M-01's prior severity, under the standing rule that a finding of the same root-cause class reappearing after a `fixed` disposition inherits at least its prior severity. Project law ranks a possible incomplete fix second only to a REGRESSION precisely because 'an incomplete fix is more dangerous than an unfixed bug, because it reads as done'. story-020 closed the `unstake` path; the identical linear-depletion drift class reaches users through the untouched `migrateIn`/`depositFor` path. classifiedFindings.label: M-05
classifiedFindings.title: stake() is not poolState-gated, so any ERC1155 holder can block finalizeAndReset and wedge the in-place migration

classification.assetImpact: Two impacts. (1) AVAILABILITY: finalizeAndReset requires totalStaked == 0 and is the ONLY transition back to Active; depositFor requires Active. A single permissionless stake during Migrating therefore blocks InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn for EVERY other parked user, for as long as the staking continues. (2) SILENT USER VALUE LOSS: accRewardPerShare is frozen during Migrating, so the contract ACCEPTS a stake it will never pay on — pendingReward == 0 is asserted in the PoC. The staker is not warned and not refused.
attackPath: 1. Operator calls initiateMigration; poolState becomes Migrating.
2. Any holder of the ERC1155 calls stake() — ungated, permissionless, a legitimate documented user action.
3. totalStaked > 0, so finalizeAndReset reverts.
4. The pool cannot return to Active, so no parked user can be migrated in.
5. ECON-02's 6-step PoC shows the re-park re-arms the timeout clock, so the loop repeats.
6. The staker who did it earns nothing — the position accrues against a frozen accRewardPerShare.
classification.likelihood: medium-to-high, and MORE LIKELY ACCIDENTAL THAN ADVERSARIAL — the timeout hatch and the stake button are both legitimate documented user actions, so an ordinary user can wedge the migration without intending to. Pure-cost griefing with zero attacker profit.
classification.assumptions: The pool is in Migrating and at least one ERC1155 unit is outside the migrator's custody.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Medium: assets are not at direct risk, but the availability of a core protocol operation (the in-place migration) is impacted by an unprivileged action, and a second leg silently costs an uninvolved user their yield for the duration. Escalated from the scanner's Low per D-10; the dedup record pre-authorised a `medium` severityCeiling. classification.assetImpact: Availability only — no value at risk. pull() is onlyOwnerOrRecipient and additionally reverts RecipientUnset when recipient == address(0).
